verdict.rationale: Obsidian Sync docs claim you can 'collaborate on a shared vault with your team' and offer version history to restore prior states, which suggests basic shared-vault collaboration (obsidian-docs-11, obsidian-docs-28). However, community evidence indicates Obsidian's sync is file-based rather than real-time conflict-resolving: a developer built a separate CRDT-based plugin specifically to add 'Google Docs style' collaboration because native tools (including the Git plugin) are 'not great for device sync or collaboration' (obsidian-comm-8), implying simultaneous edits from multiple collaborators can conflict rather than merge seamlessly. Missing for 10: native real-time conflict resolution (CRDT or operational transform) confirmed by vendor docs, and hands-on evidence that concurrent edits don't overwrite each other.
